title: How Closely Should You Follow a Trend? Atypicality and Engagement on Social Media
authors: Marc Bravin, Melanie Clegg, Reto Hofstetter, Marc Pouly, Jonah Berger

package_source.dataset_title: Replication Data for: How Closely Should You Follow a Trend? Atypicality and Engagement on Social Media

eligible_reason: No DiD. Study 1 regresses video-level engagement on continuous atypicality scores (MUVID embeddings) with fixest feglm(family = binomial, weights = plays) and author + month-year FE on a cross-section of ~85,000 TikTok trend videos; Study 4 is a within-creator field experiment (feglm engagement ~ atypical | creator_id); prestudies and Studies 2-3 are surveys and online experiments (Stata). Continuous regressor, nonlinear model, no adoption timing.
design_notes: Zip (693 MB, with duplicated entries that bsdtar rejects) extracted with a Python zipfile extractor that checks paths: 000/001 prestudies, 100_MUVID_Source_Code, 200_Study1 (Code.ipynb, Study 1 Trend Dataset.csv, .RData), 300-501 experiments (Stata do-files, raw data), 600_Study4 (Code.ipynb, 3 KB dataset), 700_MUVID_App (app, model weights, embedding indexes).
screener_notes: Ruled out from the abstract and the estimation calls. .RData, model weights and app code were not loaded or run.
main_text_note: Article confirms cross-sectional engagement models on continuous atypicality (grouped logit, binomial GLM with creator FE) and experiments; no DiD terms.
